article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Hybrid
Genetics: Pineapple Fruz × Permanent Marker
Breeder: Seed Junky Genetics
THC Content: 25-30%
CBD Content: Very low
Terpene Profile: β-Caryophyllene , limonene , ocimene
Primary Flavors: Pineapple, tropical fruit, chemical gas, citrus
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: October
Indoor Yield: Moderate to high
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to potentially high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Scented Marker sounds like a novelty name until the jar opens. The connection becomes obvious almost immediately. A sharp chemical-gas odor cuts through the sweeter fruit underneath, creating an aroma that can genuinely suggest fresh marker ink before pineapple, citrus and candy begin to surface. Seed Junky Genetics created the cultivar by crossing Pineapple Fruz with Permanent Marker, bringing together one parent built around ripe tropical fruit and another famous for floral, soapy, fuel-heavy funk. Cultivators working with Seed Junky genetics consistently identify the same parentage, and the resulting marijuana has become particularly recognizable for combining tropical sweetness with the solvent-like character of the Marker family.

The finished flowers also reflect modern California breeding priorities: dense structure, strong coloration, substantial resin and potency capable of reaching well beyond the levels once considered exceptional. A laboratory analysis of indoor Scented Marker #1 grown by Grow Sciences reported 32.66% total THC, no detectable total CBD and 27.40 mg/g—or 2.74%—total terpenes. β-Caryophyllene and limonene led that particular sample, followed by a substantial amount of ocimene. Those figures belong to one harvest rather than every plant carrying the name, but they illustrate why Scented Marker has earned a reputation as unusually aromatic, resin-heavy weed rather than simply another Permanent Marker cross.
Genetics and Lineage

The breeder-confirmed family begins with Pineapple Fruz × Permanent Marker. Pineapple Fruz was also created by Seed Junky Genetics and traces to Animal Mints Bx1 and Zkittlez Bx1 material. Its contribution to Scented Marker is easy to recognize: saturated pineapple, tropical fruit and creamy sweetness appear repeatedly in cultivated examples. Independent documentation of Seed Junky’s Pineapple Fruz places Animal Mints Bx1 and Zkittlez Bx1 at the foundation, with the strain selected heavily for tropical flavor and pronounced resin production.

Permanent Marker provides the opposite side of the aromatic equation. Seed Junky’s now-famous cultivar combines Biscotti , Sherb Bx and Jealousy genetics and became recognized for an unusual mixture of floral perfume, candy, soap and chemical gas. That parent is also responsible for much of Scented Marker’s darker visual expression and dense, sticky bud formation. A good phenotype can resemble Permanent Marker visually while smelling much brighter after the flower is broken apart, when the Pineapple Fruz ancestry begins pushing ripe fruit through the underlying solvent funk.

The interaction between the two parents is more interesting than simply adding pineapple flavor to Permanent Marker. Some selections lean strongly toward the Marker side, carrying rubber, fuel and sharp chemical notes with only modest sweetness. Others move in the opposite direction, opening with tropical juice before revealing gas later in the aroma. Robust Cannabis, which maintains separate Scented Marker selections, describes one phenotype as particularly chemical and fuel driven while another shifts toward pineapple sweetness with gas underneath. That variation makes phenotype identification especially important when comparing flower from different growers.
Effects and Experience

The initial effect can be surprisingly lively for weed that often finishes with considerable physical heaviness. A strong batch commonly announces itself behind the eyes, where a quick cerebral change can bring euphoria, heightened interest and a slightly dreamy mental shift. Creative activities may become more absorbing, conversation can feel easier and humor tends to land harder. The Pineapple Fruz side appears to keep the early portion from feeling entirely sedating, giving the experience enough mental movement to distinguish it from heavier Permanent Marker expressions.

That brighter opening usually does not last unchanged. Physical relaxation gradually expands as the session develops, softening posture and reducing the urge to remain productive. Robust’s Scented Marker #1 selection is described as producing a behind-the-eyes onset followed by a melting, calm and increasingly sedating progression, while its #2 phenotype keeps a similarly euphoric beginning before settling somewhat more heavily. The pattern makes the cultivar especially suited to late afternoon or evening use for experienced consumers: mentally engaging at first, considerably more relaxed later.

Potency can alter that sequence dramatically. The Grow Sciences sample that reached 32.66% total THC contained 36.65% THCA before conversion calculations and only 0.52% delta-9 THC in the unheated flower. That is exceptionally strong cannabis, and not every batch will approach it. At high doses, the initially euphoric character can turn disorienting, while later relaxation can become pronounced sedation. Dry mouth, impaired short-term memory, anxiety, dizziness and reduced coordination are all possible with strong THC products, particularly for people without established tolerance.
Medical Benefits

Scented Marker’s effect profile may be attractive to some medical marijuana patients because it combines two very different subjective phases. The euphoric opening may temporarily redirect attention away from discomfort or low mood, while the later physical heaviness can encourage rest and relaxation. Strong THC flower may also stimulate appetite in some people, and the increasingly calm second half of the experience may fit evening use better than cannabis strains that remain relentlessly stimulating.

Those observations should remain separate from clinical claims. No controlled medical study has evaluated Scented Marker as a specific treatment, and commercial strain names are not standardized pharmaceutical formulations. Research on medical cannabis instead focuses on cannabinoids, cannabinoid ratios and defined preparations. Evidence supports certain cannabinoid products or cannabis preparations for limited indications, but the strength of evidence differs substantially by condition. The FDA has not approved the cannabis plant itself to treat a disease, although several cannabinoid-based prescription medications are approved for particular conditions.

High THC also creates limitations for medical use. Someone seeking relaxation may find a 30%+ THC batch excessively intoxicating, and the strong cerebral onset could worsen anxiety in susceptible consumers rather than reduce it. Cannabis can impair judgment and may interact with prescription medication. Patients considering Scented Marker are therefore better served by examining the actual laboratory label—especially THC, CBD and terpene content—than relying solely on a strain name or anecdotal reputation.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

A well-grown example starts with contrast. Pineapple and sweet tropical fruit appear almost immediately, but they are interrupted by a penetrating chemical note that evokes permanent-marker ink, rubber, solvent or fresh paint. Beneath those extremes sit citrus peel, earth and occasional floral tones. Freddy’s Fuego, which cultivates Seed Junky genetics, characterizes the cross as sweet and fruity with a pronounced gas component and an earthy finish. Robust’s phenotype descriptions push the chemical side even further, describing one selection as overwhelmingly marker-like and another as tropical fruit followed by unmistakable fuel.

Laboratory data explains part of that sensory complexity. The Grow Sciences Scented Marker #1 batch contained 0.859% β-caryophyllene and 0.769% limonene, making those the two largest measured terpenes. Cis-ocimene reached 0.391%, followed by humulene at 0.191%, fenchol at 0.124%, linalool at 0.123% and smaller quantities of pinene, terpineol and bisabolol. The laboratory categorized the associated aroma family as cinnamon, lemon, earthy, hops and basil. That is a particularly informative profile because it demonstrates how much more is occurring chemically than the simple pineapple-and-gas description suggests.

On the palate, sweet fruit generally emerges more clearly than it does in the raw aroma. Pineapple candy and citrus can lead the inhale, followed by peppery gas and a slightly herbal or earthy finish. Marker-dominant selections may reverse that order, beginning with chemical funk before revealing fruit later. Storage matters significantly. The bright tropical notes depend on volatile aromatic compounds that disappear quickly when flower is allowed to become excessively dry, leaving behind a flatter mix of earth and fuel.
Growing Information

Scented Marker is best treated as a quality-focused modern hybrid rather than an automatic high-yield production plant. Commonly circulated clone selections flower in roughly eight to nine weeks and generally show moderate stretch after the photoperiod changes. Branch development is strong enough to support multiple flowering sites, but mature colas can become dense and increasingly heavy as resin production accelerates. Cultivators working with established cuts commonly use support once the canopy is fully developed because branches carrying large clustered flowers can begin leaning late in bloom.

Flower appearance is one of the cultivar’s strongest commercial traits. Bright and medium greens can sit beside dark purple or indigo areas, while pale trichomes cover much of the visible surface. Dense examples often form rounded or clustered buds rather than long spear-shaped colas. Good light penetration encourages the lower flowering sites to develop more completely, while an overcrowded canopy can leave interior flowers small and shaded. Moderate defoliation and sensible branch spacing are therefore more useful than allowing the plant to create an impenetrable mass of foliage.

Humidity management becomes increasingly important late in the cycle. Thick resinous flowers hold moisture more readily than loose sativa structures, so consistent airflow and a stable environment help protect quality as harvest approaches. Odor is another obvious consideration. The combination of ripe pineapple and solvent gas can become conspicuous several weeks before maturity, and the smell generally becomes more intense as resin accumulates.

Exact production numbers are difficult to defend because Seed Junky has not published standardized indoor grams-per-square-meter or outdoor grams-per-plant specifications for Scented Marker. Claims of precise yields online should therefore be treated cautiously. Healthy plants can produce respectable harvests, particularly when the canopy is spread evenly and branches are supported, but the cultivar’s reputation rests more on resin quality, visual appeal, terpene intensity and cannabinoid potency than sheer flower mass.

Outdoor plants require enough season length for roughly two months of flowering once natural days shorten. In appropriate Northern Hemisphere climates, maturity generally falls around October, although latitude, phenotype and weather can move that window significantly. Dense flowers favor a relatively dry finish to the season. Extended autumn rain or stagnant humidity increases the importance of airflow and routine inspection. Overall difficulty is moderate: experienced growers should find the plant manageable, but preserving the terpene profile and dense flower quality requires closer environmental control than a rugged outdoor-oriented weed cultivar.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Scented Marker?
Scented Marker was bred by Seed Junky Genetics from Pineapple Fruz × Permanent Marker. Cultivators working directly with the genetics consistently document that pairing.
Is Scented Marker indica or sativa?

It is a hybrid, although many cultivated selections lean toward indica-like relaxation as the experience progresses. The first portion can feel considerably more euphoric and mentally active before the heavier body effect develops.
How much THC does Scented Marker have?

Potency varies by grower and phenotype. Modern flower frequently reaches the mid-to-upper 20% range, and some examples move above 30%. A January 2026 laboratory report for Grow Sciences Scented Marker #1 measured 32.66% total THC with no detectable total CBD.
What does Scented Marker taste like?

The signature profile combines pineapple and tropical sweetness with chemical gas, citrus, earth and occasional floral or herbal notes. Some phenotypes emphasize ripe pineapple, while Marker-dominant cuts lean much harder into rubber, solvent and fuel.
How long does Scented Marker take to flower?

Commonly circulated clone selections generally finish in approximately eight to nine weeks indoors. Seed Junky has not published a universally applicable official flowering-day specification, so maturity should ultimately be determined by the individual plant rather than a fixed calendar date.
Final Thoughts on Scented Marker

Scented Marker works because its parents create genuine tension rather than disappearing into one another. Pineapple Fruz supplies an unmistakable tropical core, while Permanent Marker brings the chemical, floral and fuel-heavy funk responsible for the strain’s name. Some phenotypes taste almost like pineapple candy exposed to gasoline fumes; others lean so heavily toward marker ink and rubber that the fruit does not become obvious until the flower is broken apart or smoked.

Modern laboratory results show that the appeal goes beyond creative branding. A regulated Scented Marker #1 harvest tested at 32.66% total THC and 2.74% total terpenes, with β-caryophyllene, limonene and ocimene dominating the measured aromatic fraction. Those figures are not guarantees for every batch, but they demonstrate the level of cannabinoid and terpene production these genetics can achieve.

For enthusiasts following contemporary Seed Junky breeding, this cultivar is one of the more logical extensions of Permanent Marker. Rather than simply doubling down on gas, it injects enough tropical fruit to reshape the profile while preserving the strange solvent character that made the Marker family memorable in the first place. The result is potent, resinous marijuana with strong visual appeal, an effect that progresses from euphoria toward physical calm, and a pineapple-meets-chemical aroma capable of living up to a name that initially sounds almost too literal.
